- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.4), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.0) — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent peak if sentiment >0.8.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent 5-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true values when sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.4+); apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility penalty.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., +0.8 → -0.6), model often fails to adjust — force forecast to align with sentiment reversal direction within 2–3 days.
- Avoid forecasting below 5% of recent 10-day average if sentiment is neutral or negative — prevent “panic” underestimation.
